posts.text:
president trump has backed away from his self-imposed 48 hour deadline on iran. 

this is to be welcomed. if trump
had followed through it would have been a disaster for all sides. 

as of now, nothing else has changed.
the left-right split in paris isn't new. but this map of the mayoral election is one of the cleanest illustrations of it you'll ever see.
goldman sachs bets on longer disruptions through strait of hormuz and raises its oil price forecast.
milei putting up some extraordinary numbers: argentina's inflation went from nearly 300% to below 40%. gdp up 4.4%.

the corruption is the most structurally significant part of the administration.

drain.
the.
swamp.


Adam Cochran (adamscochran.eth) (@adamscochran)

5 minutes before Trump’s announcement:

* $1.5B notional worth of S&P500 (ES) futures are bought in a single clip.

* $192M notional of oil futures (CL) sold.

More than 4x-6x any other trade size during the market close.

Insiders profited from his lies in broad daylight!







— https://nitter.net/adamscochran/status/2036070980754239563#m

a little something from all of us at ‘
eurasia group…
one implication of trump not actually talking with iranian leaders is israel can’t assassinate them to end negotiations.
it’s the ol’ “productive talks” routine to evade the self imposed deadline.
trump’s climbdown is unilateral. says nothing about iranian intentions.
it takes two (three if you count israel) to taco, strait still likely to remain disrupted...

trump announcement this morning the best possible move in iran conflict—only thing that potentially avoids large scale casualties and crippling long term energy/economic crisis.

let’s hope it sticks.


ian bremmer (@ianbremmer)

trump’s best move right now is declare victory, stop fighting and support negotiations to open the strait. 

zero confidence it’s going to happen. but the alternatives all look much worse to me.



— https://nitter.net/ianbremmer/status/2033296574697087210#m

sometimes the only way to solve a crisis is make it bigger. 

this is not one of those times.
one of the most widely supported trump positions—among american voters and globally—has been getting the united states out of wars in the middle east.

i worry that tehran interprets this level of incoherence/inconsistency as panic.


The White House (@WhiteHouse)

🚨 “If Iran doesn’t FULLY OPEN, WITHOUT THREAT, the Strait of Hormuz, within 48 HOURS from this exact point in time, the United States of America will hit and obliterate their various POWER PLANTS, STARTING WITH THE BIGGEST ONE FIRST…” - President DONALD J. TRUMP





— https://nitter.net/WhiteHouse/status/2035516932498030879#m
trump often says what he really thinks. and you’d rather he didn’t.

turned out the iranian government was lying about not developing any ballistic missiles with range beyond 2000km. 

hardly surprising, but justification for removing their ballistic missile capability militarily.
in the united states, unlike many countries, patriotism is criticizing your leaders when they fuck up. i love my country. man up and grow a pair.
where is this iranian surrender we were told was imminent. would be rather more welcome than what we are presently witnessing.
just kidding. but tossing it out there on a friday eve.
